STEP 1 - Scene: This is a buffet-style mixed plate. It holds a fried chicken sandwich, a barbecue pork rib, fried chicken pieces and three pieces of crab sushi roll.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A dinner plate, about 26 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Chicken sandwich (bun plus breaded patty)
- BBQ pork rib section
- Fried chicken pieces (2–3)
- California roll pieces (1)
- Baked/torched crab sushi pieces (2)

STEP 4 - Area (food covers about 51% of the plate):

| Item | Share of plate | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Sandwich | 20% | 106 cm² |
| Rib | 12% | 64 cm² |
| Fried chicken | 12% | 64 cm² |
| California roll | 2.5% | 13 cm² |
| Baked rolls | 4.5% | 24 cm² |

STEP 5 - Volume:

| Item | Area × height | Gross volume |
|---|---|---|
| Sandwich | 106 cm² × 5 cm | 530 ml |
| Rib | 64 cm² × 2.5 cm | 160 ml |
| Fried chicken | 64 cm² × 3 cm | 192 ml |
| California roll | 13 cm² × 3 cm | 39 ml |
| Baked rolls | 24 cm² × 3 cm | 72 ml |

STEP 6 - Grams:
- **Sandwich:** The bun is airy and the patty is dense, so I used a blended density of about 0.35. 530 ml × 0.35 ≈ 185 g.
- **Rib:** Includes bone, so density 0.75. 160 ml × 0.75 = 120 g.
- **Fried chicken:** 192 ml × 0.6 = 115 g.
- **California roll:** 39 ml × 0.8 ≈ 30 g.
- **Baked rolls:** 72 ml × 0.8 ≈ 58 g.

STEP 7 - Energy (kcal per 100 g):

| Item | Grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sandwich | 185 g | 260 | 481 kcal |
| Rib (with bone) | 120 g | 280 | 336 kcal |
| Fried chicken | 115 g | 280 | 322 kcal |
| California roll | 30 g | 150 | 45 kcal |
| Baked rolls | 58 g | 200 | 116 kcal |

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 508 g and 1,300 kcal. That is plausible for a heavy buffet plate with mostly fried foods.
